description: N5/C3 pre-implementation design challenge (approvals + human exception queue)

binding_strength.instructions: The design binds an approval to exactly one operation, so an approval granted for one action cannot be replayed, reused or repointed at another action, subject or parameter set

criteria.true: The request carries tenant, branch, action type, a digest of the protected parameters, requester, required authority, risk class, expiry and correlation id, and execution is refused when the presented digest differs
criteria.false: A granted approval can authorize a different operation, a different subject, or parameters the approver never saw

stale_authority.instructions: The design prevents an unused approval from remaining usable after the approver's authority changes, and prevents approval authority from being inferred from UI role labels or request bodies

criteria.true: Approver authority is resolved from a trusted server-side directory at decision time and re-resolved at execution time, so revocation, suspension, expiry or a sponsor change invalidates the unused approval
criteria.false: A revoked, expired or unverified approver keeps an approval valid, or role labels / body fields can supply approval authority

agent_boundary.instructions: The design prevents an agent (bounded automation identity) from approving anything, including its own proposal or another agent's proposal, and prevents agent self-approval through any indirection

criteria.true: Only a human account with live required authority can decide, an agent actor is refused as an approver, and a proposal by an agent identity remains subject to human approval
criteria.false: An agent actor can decide, or two agents can satisfy each other's approval requirement

unknown_outcome.instructions: The design keeps an unevidenced or unknown external outcome unknown, instead of converting it into success or failure

criteria.true: An unknown/unevidenced execution result is recorded as unknown and moves the request to a human-required state, and a later definitive outcome for the same attempt is refused without evidence
criteria.false: An unevidenced outcome can be recorded as succeeded or failed, or a missing provider result is scored as success or failure

exception_queue_integrity.instructions: The human exception queue is owned work rather than an unowned record: every case carries the reason automation stopped, the evidence requirement, SLA ownership in the existing task/helpdesk system, and closure rules that require evidence when evidence is required

criteria.true: Each case links to a task/helpdesk work item that owns assignment, due date, escalation and follow-up, carries a closed kind and severity, and cannot be closed without evidence when evidence is required or while the resolution is unknown
criteria.false: A case can exist without an owner, be closed by anyone without required evidence, or be resolved as unknown and still closed

state_machine_integrity.instructions: The approval state machine is explicit, with an enumerated legal-transition set, refused illegal jumps, terminal states that cannot silently move, and idempotent retries that reconcile the original operation instead of duplicating it

criteria.true: Every transition is enumerated; illegal jumps and terminal moves are refused in both the domain layer and the database; a repeated idempotency key returns the original record and a divergent reuse is refused
criteria.false: States can be skipped, terminal states can change, or retries create duplicate approvals, decisions or executions

tenant_branch_isolation.instructions: The design prevents cross-tenant and cross-branch approval, decision, execution or exception access, including through identifiers supplied in a request body or query string

criteria.true: Tenant and branch scope come only from verified session authority, every read and write is scoped, and row-level security plus a cross-branch authority check refuse foreign scope
criteria.false: A caller can read, decide, execute or open a case across a tenant or branch boundary it does not hold

activity_authority_confusion.instructions: The design keeps the derived operational activity feed (human + agent activity) from becoming approval or execution authority

criteria.true: Activity rows are projected from approval truth and hold no path that can authorize, approve, execute or mutate a request
criteria.false: A derived activity record can be used as, or mutated into, approval or execution state

audit_completeness.instructions: For an important protected action, the recorded C3 trail is sufficient to reconstruct who or what proposed it, under which tenant and branch, which authority and policy applied, who approved or rejected it, what was executed, what receipt returned and what canonical outcome or exception resulted

criteria.true: Proposal, requirement, decision, execution, receipt and exception rows are append-only or transition-guarded, correlated, and enough to reconstruct the decision chain
criteria.false: A material step of the approval or exception chain is unrecorded, unattributed or not correlatable

residual_implementation_risk.instructions: How much residual risk remains in this design before it is safe to implement as a bounded synthetic slice

weakest_control.instructions: Which single control is the weakest in this design and most likely to be defeated by a realistic input

criteria.binding: The binding of the approval to one operation and one parameter set
criteria.authority: Resolving and re-resolving the approver's live authority
criteria.unknown: Keeping an unknown external outcome unknown
criteria.exception: Exception queue ownership, evidence and closure rules
criteria.state: State machine, terminal states and idempotency
criteria.activity: Keeping derived activity from becoming authority
